newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares firm as market ponders profits.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares firm as market ponders profits.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed from weakness at the opening on Tuesday, and traders said prices would hover near current levels through the week as the market consolidated from its recent quick climb.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 474.67, down less than a quarter of a percent from its previous close of 475.54. It was at 360 a month ago.
Market leader national power company UES had edged up to $0.4270 at 0848 GMT from a morning low of $0.4240 and $0.4285 at the previous close.

After almost two hours of trade, only three shares had topped $1 million reported turnover. Oil company Surgutneftegaz prefs, one of the most traded shares, hovered nearing opening levels at $0.650 from $0.655 on Monday.
Brunswick director Martin Diggle said some Russian buying was giving the market tone but it was not clear what time horizon the investors had or when they might sell.
He said the market would rise or fall by up to five percent through the week as it consolidated at the post-boom level after a month of strong gains with some Western profit-taking.
"This is a typical healthy consolidation -- the market really needs it," he said. "People want to wait and see if there is going to be a takeoff again."
Creditanstalt sales director Tad Berger said the market could end up a few percent by the end of the week but would stay in a fairly narrow trading range.
Russia's leading 10 to 15 shares account for about 75 percent of daily turnover, which has been drying up recently, he said.

But he said regional telecoms and energos were seeing demand. The Grant-100 index CAIC, which includes fairly illiquid shares, has dipped less than narrower leading indexes, closing on Monday at 1223.17 off Wednesday's record 1244.13.
